labels.reason: Historical reviewer: Two distinct FP clusters. (1) 'in a world where' is a legitimate historical/technical contrast phrase when not used as a rhetorical opener ('Mainframe-style arrays were designed in a world where a single mainframe...'; Paul Graham literary use; PEP technical contrast). (2) 'In conclusion' / 'in conclusion' is a standard section marker in legal opinions, medical abstracts, academic Q&A, and 19th-century literary prose — not slop in those contexts. 'Now more than ever' fired on a Keats poem. 'It's important to note' is more consistently sloppy but fires on legitimate technical doc signaling (MDN, PEP).

original.excerpt: [legal/courtlistener] (Prohibited phrase found: "In conclusion". Rewrite ) In conclusion, we hold that if the Act is to be fairly administered, it should be interpreted so as to preclude a finding that child-support payments are income to two households.
